title: Game Narrator profile manifest (.gnprofile.json)
description: A portable profile revision: edition identity, source provenance pointers, the dialogue graph, regions, approved voice mappings (1.1) and publication state. Closed object: an unknown key is a typo or a version skew, and silently ignoring either is how a profile imports with content nobody reviewed (docs/spec/14). Copyrighted source bytes never appear here; sources carry a SHA-256 and a rights state, and text whose rights are unsettled is null with a reason. Voice reference audio is the same: the manifest carries the SHA-256, and the bytes travel only inside an acknowledged .gnpack (ADR-0101).
$comment: Every content section is required. An absent section and an empty one mean different things ('characters were not considered' vs 'this revision has no characters'), and the exporter always writes [] for a section with no rows — see canonical.go's note on empty sections. Requiring the key makes that distinction impossible to lose in transit.

schema_version.description: Compatibility version of this document shape. A reader that does not know a version refuses it rather than ignoring fields it has never seen. 1.1 adds the voices section and publication.narrator_fallback (ADR-0101).

profile_id.description: The revision row this document was exported from. Carried for cross-checking; a re-import mints its own and does not reuse it.

manifest_digest.description: SHA-256 over the canonical JSON projection of this document with the digest itself, profile_id and the publication section removed, and every row id replaced by a content-derived alias. Stable across re-import by construction; see internal/profileio/canonical.go.

RedactedReason.description: Why a message's text is null. Absent means the text is present; a redacted message must say which rule withheld it, so a reviewer can tell 'unknown rights' from 'no source registered' from 'nothing wrong here'.

title.description: Title family name as the curator reads it.

slug.description: Names the game row on re-import. games.Validate's slug grammar.

tags.description: games.Game.user_tags: user labels, never a controlled vocabulary.

region.description: Release region. Compatibility is checked against a target edition on import.

language.description: BCP-47 tag of the script, not a guess from its characters (docs/spec/04).

revision.description: Script/dump revision of the edition, e.g. 'demo' or a US version marker.

aspect.description: editions.display_aspect: a positive ratio or null while the capture target is unknown.

identity.description: editions.source_identity: hash of the exact image the edition was observed against.

publication.description: Lifecycle of the exported revision. Excluded from manifest_digest: a re-import is a draft by construction, and an approval timestamp is not content. narrator_fallback rides here rather than in a content section because it is a row property of the exported profile (the import applies it to the draft it creates), the way preferred_voice_id travels.

revision.description: profiles.revision_num: which revision of the edition this was.

parent_revision.description: The revision this one was derived from, or null for the first of a lineage.

author.description: Who published it, as the publication audit recorded it.

narrator_fallback.description: profiles.narrator_fallback (ADR-0101): when a line's speaker has no approved voice, the narrator voice speaks the line if and only if this is true. A re-import applies it to the draft it creates; the import's default when absent is true, the column's DEFAULT 1.

store_digest.description: profiles.manifest_digest as the store computed it. Audit only: it hashes row ids and so does not survive the re-import that manifest_digest is built to survive.

source.description: Provenance pointer. The bytes themselves live in the asset store and travel only in an explicitly acknowledged .gnpack (docs/spec/14).

sha256.description: Content address of the payload; empty for a manual note with no bytes.

parser.description: adapter-id@semver: the importer build whose output these rows are (docs/spec/04).

uri.description: Where it came from, for audit. Never opened (docs/spec/14 'Filesystem/import').

coverage.description: Importer notes: what it saw, what it skipped.

retrieved_at.description: When the bytes were obtained. Carried and restored, because re-importing does not re-retrieve anything.

role.description: Open data by design: roles belong to a game, not to the core (docs/spec/04).

voice_profile_id.description: The approved voice this character speaks with, when the voices section carries one (ADR-0101): the cross-reference that lets a reader answer 'does this character have a voice' without joining the section by character. Null when the manifest carries no voice for the character.

rect.description: Normalized frame fractions in [0,1]; the box itself is checked in Go, because 'x + w <= 1' is not something this validator subset states.

ocr.description: Engine settings as open data (docs/spec/04 'visual profiles').

page.description: One display page. index is message_pages.ordinal, 1-based: a message can have several pages and a page is not an utterance (docs/spec/02 'Core data distinctions').

text.description: Null exactly when the parent message is redacted.

message.description: Canonical source text plus its renderings. Not an occurrence, not a page, not an utterance. original_text, normalized_text, speech_text and every page's text are null together when the source's rights do not allow shipping them, with redacted_reason naming which rule applied.

source_message_id.description: Source-side identity: the key a re-import reconciles against.

speech_text.description: Empty string means 'deliberately not spoken'; null means 'withheld' (docs/spec/02).

markup.description: Control-byte AST with source offsets; never regex-stripped text (docs/spec/02).

attribution.description: A speaker claim and how far to trust it. 'unknown' beside a speaker_id and null beside 'confirmed' are both meaningful; only 'rejected' beside a speaker_id contradicts itself, and that is refused in Go.

message_edge.description: One dialogue transition. condition is data-only: nothing here, and nothing in SQLite, evaluates it (docs/spec/02, docs/spec/05).

speaker_assertion.description: A candidate speaker that is not the resolved one (docs/spec/02 keeps these apart from messages.speaker_id because a name on screen is not proof).

reviewer.description: Required for a manual method, absent for an automated one — a rule that spans two fields, so it lives in games.SpeakerAssertion.Validate.

voice.description: One approved voice revision (ADR-0101). The id is the voice_profiles id, unmodified by a re-import: the Base registry names a voice from it, and the shared registry is the reason it is stable where every other row id is not. The reference WAV bytes live in the asset store and travel only inside a .gnpack; a pointer whose bytes are absent on import is reported, not written.

id.description: The voice_profiles id. Stable across re-imports on purpose: the registry name and the speech cache key derive from it.

character.description: A character this manifest defines, or 'narrator' — the runtime's constant speaker for unattributed lines, not a roster row. A re-import remaps the roster ids and passes the narrator through.

revision.description: The revision number. The registry name derives from it, so a re-import preserves rather than renumbers it.

state.description: Only approved revisions travel: the reference they froze is the only thing a re-import could register, and a draft row has no reference at all.

reference_sha256.description: Content address of the approved reference WAV. The pack carries blobs/<sha256>; a default export is the pointer alone.

ref_transcript.description: The exact transcript of the reference clip, frozen at approval.

model_id.description: The Base checkpoint model identity the cache keys carry.

language.description: BCP-47 tag the synthesis requests name.

fingerprint.description: SHA-256 over (reference digest, transcript, model): the revision identity every TTS cache key for this voice names.

gain.description: The per-voice output gain (0..10, the store's column bound; 1 is unity). Checked in Go beside the store's CHECK.

design_instruction.description: The design brief that shaped the voice. Carried for the audit; the import never re-designs from it.

consent_provenance.description: docs/spec/14's consent record, frozen at approval. Required on the wire: a voice that arrived without the consent that licensed it is refused.

approved_by.description: Who approved the revision, as the approval audit recorded it.

approved_at.description: When the approval happened, at the approving appliance. Dropped from the digest projection like the publication section: an audit moment, not content.
